title: All-fibrant Brown axioms and partial-limit Reedy diagram predicates
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category with independent object and morphism universes, an object $1$, and arrow classes $W,F$. The all-fibrant Brown predicate means: $1$ is terminal; $W,F$ contain all isomorphisms; $W$ satisfies two-out-of-three and is closed under composition; $F$ is closed under composition; all arrows $X\to1$ lie in $F$; pullbacks of $F$-maps along arbitrary arrows exist and lie in $F$; base change preserves $F\cap W$; and each arrow factors as $w$ followed by $p$ with $w\in W$, $p\in F$, without functorial choices.
For any ordinary category $K$ and $k\in K$, let $B_k$ be the opposite of the existing nonidentity slice over $k^{\mathrm{op}}$ from [lem-coef-direct-wfs-extension], with codomain projection $B_k\to K$. Equivalently its objects are nonidentity arrows $k\to j$, with all commuting triangles under $k$ as morphisms; parallel arrows remain distinct. The outgoing arrows define a cone of apex $X_k$ over $X|_{B_k}$. A strict diagram $X:K\to\mathcal C$ is Reedy fibrant if each matching limit exists and the induced arrow $X_k\to\lim_{B_k}X$ lies in $F$. For a transformation $f:X\to Y$, its relative matching test in a class $P$ asserts existence of both matching limits, of their relative pullback $Q_k=M_kX\times_{M_kY}Y_k$, and membership in $P$ of the unique arrow $X_k\to Q_k$ whose projections are the matching arrow and $f_k$. A Reedy fibration is a transformation between Reedy fibrant diagrams satisfying this test in $F$ at every $k$. The full category of Reedy fibrant diagrams inherits these fibrations and componentwise $W$ as weak equivalences. For a functor $J\to K$, restriction preserves Reedy diagrams and fibrations, including trivial ones, when precomposition preserves Reedy fibrant objects, Reedy fibrations, and componentwise weak equivalences among the latter. Its inclusion into strict diagrams induces the degreewise lifted nerve map, using the universe-lifted nerve of [def-coef-coherent-localization-interface]. All predicates use actual limiting cones and pullback squares; no ambient completeness is required.
